panels.title: Accuracy Reward
notes: Panel 'Accuracy Reward' of a 1 x 3 strip. A thick polyline (the smoothed curve, taupe (#B8A898)) over a pale filled area, plus one semi-transparent dot per logged point (light taupe, semi-transparent (#DDD3C9 on white)) drawn under the line. No legend, no x tick labels, no axis titles; the y tick labels are printed left of a grey spine, with dashed gridlines at the ticks.

Series names are not printed. 'Accuracy Reward' (the panel title) names the smoothed line; 'Accuracy Reward (raw points)' names the raw dots. x is the ordinal position of the point, 1..30 from left to right (the x axis carries no ticks or numbers; the caption says only that 'the rewards are plotted every five steps').

Measured on the PDF's embedded bitmap (page 21, one RGB image 3118 x 573 px for the whole strip, 7.87 px per PDF point; no vector paths, no text layer). Y calibration: least squares through the 4 dashed gridlines, whose centres coincide with the centres of the printed tick labels to <= 1 px: value = 3.08232 -0.0043327 * y_native (230.8 px per unit); fit residual <= 0.0013 axis units.

Line: the centreline of the stroke was fitted as a straight segment between consecutive points (max deviation of any column from its segment 0.33 px); a vertex is the mean of the two adjacent segment fits at the vertex x. The 30 vertices sit on an even x grid, native x = 155.0 + 29.15 * (k - 1) px (rms deviation of the sharp vertices from the grid <= 0.08 px). Estimated error of the line values: +/- 0.005 axis units (about 1 px).

Dots: 17 px discs; the centre was found by fitting a disc of that radius at the vertex x to the dot-coloured pixels not covered by the line. All 30 dots are individually resolvable; those more than 80% hidden under the line (visible share in brackets) carry confidence 0.7: points 1 (14%), 3 (7%), 23 (9%). Estimated error: +/- 0.005 axis units, about twice that for the low-visibility dots.

Cross-check with a known relation: in all three panels the smoothed value at point k equals the mean of raw points k and k-1 (a 2-point moving average), and at point 1 it equals raw point 1. Residual of that relation here: largest 0.0042, mean 0.0024 axis units (1.0 px); point 1: 0.0001. This confirms both readings, including the dots that are mostly hidden.
Y axis: tick labels printed 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5; the spine runs from 0.734 (x axis line) to 2.744 (top end), used as axes.y.range. Crop px of the first and last vertex: [25.6, 88.3], [186.5, 33.4].

uncertain: The x axis prints nothing: no tick marks, no tick labels, no axis title (axes.x.ticks and range are null). 'Value at each x tick position' therefore does not exist for this figure; the truth records every vertex of the smoothed line instead, keyed by x = 1..30 (ordinal position, left to right). The caption ('plotted every five steps') suggests the points are 5 training steps apart, but neither the first step nor the scale is printed, so step numbers (5, 10, ... or 0, 5, ...) would be a guess and were not used. A prediction that keys its points by step number, by 0-based index or by a 0-1 fraction will not pair with these rows in the scorer (x floats must be equal); only the count and the values are comparable in that case.

Series names are not printed (no legend). The smoothed line is named after the panel title and the dots '<title> (raw points)'. With two truth series the scorer requires series names to match (they are ignored only when both sides have a single series): a prediction with one series named after the panel title pairs with the smoothed line (the 30 raw rows then count as missing); a prediction naming its series 'smoothed' / 'raw' or similar does not pair at all. Drop the '(raw points)' rows from the truth if only the line is to be scored.

kind 'line' with orientation 'vertical': the scorer normalises by axes.y.range, the measured extent of the y spine (not round numbers: the plotting library chose the limits), i.e. 2.01, 1.56 and 103.2 axis units for panels a, b, c.

Smoothed line vs raw dots differ systematically by about 0.5 px (0.002 in a/b, 0.1 in c) from the exact 2-point mean; either reading may carry that half-pixel bias. It is far below the scorer's tolerance.
No axis titles are printed: axes.y.name is null (the quantity is the panel title).

figure.bbox is copied verbatim from the picture's prov in document.json (l, t, r, b with coord_origin BOTTOMLEFT, as in the existing truth files); bbox_px is in pixels of the bundle crop. The crop cuts about 2.5 pt off the left and 3 pt off the bottom of the embedded image; panel boxes are thirds of the image clamped to the crop.
